svg.text: Volts, Amps, Ohms and Watts in a Wire
Electrons flowing round a circuit are like water flowing round a pipe
Atoms get in the way: electrons
bump into them and the wire heats up
Heat given out each second = power P = I × V (watts)
I · current = electrons passing this line each second
Flow = litres passing this line each second
More push (V) → more flow (I). More resistance (R) → less flow (I).
Power P in watts = current × voltage: how fast the energy is handed over.
Electrons are not used up: in one loop the current is the same everywhere.
What they lose is energy, which the resistor gives out as heat (or light in a bulb).
